name: spex-machina
description: The spec state machine. A standalone CLI that owns the structural half of spec-driven development: typed graph specs, merkle-based change tracking, deterministic impact analysis, and bead task mapping.

requirements.name: Validate spec structure
requirements.description: Given a spec directory, confirm it is a valid DAG with no cycles and no broken references, that every declared content path resolves, and that coverage holds in both directions — every component described by a test_section, every requirement derived and implemented. Structured error output.

requirements.name: Compute merkle tree
requirements.description: Hash every node, store snapshots, diff against previous snapshots, classify change impact paths.

requirements.name: Map spec nodes to beads
requirements.description: Each plan-relevant spec node maps to a bead with spec_id, typed dependencies, and full metadata (requirements, component, module, spec_hash, proposal). Plan-relevant is a closed set of node types — component, data_flow and test_section, plus one epic per proposal — and a mapping record points at a node in that set, never at prose that elaborates one.

requirements.name: Compute impact
requirements.description: Given changed spec nodes, find all affected beads and classify actions (create/obsolete/retarget).

requirements.name: Apply changes
requirements.description: Turn a merkle diff into applied tracker state through plan, an external adapter, and ingest. Plan composes a tool-agnostic changeset — create, close and retarget operations plus the absorbed entries of marked cosmetic modifications — carrying deterministic bead-type assignment, parent hierarchy under the proposal epic, lineage deps, priority propagation, and a per-op idempotency label keyed to the journal event the op's receipt will reference. An adapter outside the binary executes the ops against a bead tracker and writes receipts. Ingest appends the run's change events and task receipts to the task journal from the changeset and receipts, then saves the snapshot when the run is complete. spex itself never invokes a bead CLI.

requirements.name: Manage proposals
requirements.description: Register proposals, validate structure, link to spec changes and bead actions, show history.

requirements.name: Render spec
requirements.description: Generate markdown, DOT, or JSON from spec structure.

requirements.name: Self-hosting
requirements.description: Spex Machina's own spec is managed by Spex Machina (after bootstrap).

requirements.name: Deterministic
requirements.description: Given the same spec state and snapshot, always produce the same diff, impact, and actions. No LLM calls.

requirements.name: Composable
requirements.description: Every subcommand reads stdin or files, writes stdout or files, and exits with a small set of documented codes: 0 is success, and every non-zero code is documented by the surface that owns it — input error, contract refusal, diff errors present, not a spex project. A caller branches on the code, never by grepping a message. Pipeable.

requirements.name: Fast
requirements.description: Validating a spec with 100 modules and 1000 nodes should take less than 1 second.

requirements.name: Git-native
requirements.description: Snapshots are files committed to git. Proposals are files committed to git. No external state.

requirements.name: Spec test strategy
requirements.description: Spec format supports test_sections at module level and test_plan at project level, enabling traceability from components to verification scenarios.

requirements.name: CLI infrastructure
requirements.description: Declarative subcommand registration via cobra, auto-generated help for every subcommand, version info via ldflags, shell completions, and consistent error handling.

requirements.name: Coupled sections
requirements.description: Project.json supports a sections array with typed entries. Sections with type 'coupled' require a corresponding module and a section.schema.json in the module's spec directory. Spex validates the envelope generically and delegates content validation to the module's schema.

requirements.name: Data flow contract layer
requirements.description: Data flows are cross-component contracts that describe the shapes moving between components in a module's uses graph. When a data flow's content (its Data Shapes section) changes, spex creates a dedicated task bead parented under the proposal epic, and participating component beads (via the flow's uses array) gain depends edges on it. The data_flow bead is implemented first: shared types and interfaces are updated across all participants, the codebase compiles, and tests or logic that need per-component follow-up are marked with deferred-work markers naming the specific component bead that will resolve them. Each participating component bead then updates only the files it owns and removes the deferred markers pointing to itself. This prevents cross-bead cascading edits that otherwise produce unowned TODO markers across the codebase.

requirements.name: No runtime subprocesses
requirements.description: The spex spec pipeline invokes no external subprocesses: all interaction with external tools (bead trackers, git) happens via input/output data artifacts. User-owned adapter scripts — outside the spex binary — bridge artifacts to the bead tracker. Callers supply state (git HEAD, bead list) as file or stdin inputs. The sole sanctioned exception, outside every pipeline path, is spex upgrade driving the embedded installer synchronously.

requirements.name: Declared stack
requirements.description: The implementation stack is a declared contract, not a convention. The language is Go, at or above the version the `go` directive in go.mod declares; go.mod carries no `toolchain` directive, so that directive is a minimum floor and not a pin. The standard library is the default for every capability: a third-party module is admissible only where the standard library offers no viable equivalent, and each admitted module is named in this requirement together with the capability it supplies. Permitted today — github.com/spf13/cobra for subcommand registration, flag parsing, help and shell completions; github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 for JSON Schema validation of project.json, module.json and the task journal's lines; golang.org/x/term for terminal detection when a command chooses human-readable over machine-readable output. The direct requires of go.mod are to be exactly that set, and admitting, dropping or repurposing a dependency is a spec change made here first. Nothing automated enforces any of this: the check is a person reading go.mod's direct requires against the list above, and a `go get` that adds a direct require without amending this requirement is precisely the drift the requirement exists to make visible.

requirements.name: Delivery pipeline
requirements.description: spex has an automated, reproducible release pipeline that turns a version tag into signed, checksummed, provenance-attested, cross-architecture binaries, with the GoReleaser configuration and the workflow files as the source of truth for how a release is built.

requirements.name: Installable and self-updating
requirements.description: Pre-built signed binaries for linux and macOS (amd64, arm64), installable via a verified install script and go install, and updatable in place with spex upgrade.

requirements.name: Project initialization and health
requirements.description: A spex project has a declared state directory holding what the tool writes, created by an explicit init command — never implicitly, and never as a side effect of a read command. Absence of that state is an error rather than a fallback, distinguishing a project that was never initialised from one that is broken. The project's condition is diagnosable without repair: a doctor command reports what is present, missing or unreadable and names the command that would fix each finding, but never mints or moves a baseline.

modules.name: schema
modules.description: JSON Schema definitions for project.json, module.json and the task journal, plus the identity-hash function module-scoped node ids are derived from. The foundation that defines what a valid spec looks like.

modules.name: validator
modules.description: Spec directory validation: JSON schema conformance, content path resolution, DAG acyclicity, ID uniqueness.

modules.name: merkle
modules.description: Merkle hash tree over the spec: leaf hashes, interior hashes, snapshots, diff, and impact classification.

modules.name: plan
modules.description: Decides the next bead-action changeset deterministically, in one pass from the merkle diff: reads bead metadata, matches changed nodes against the task journal, classifies actions (create, obsolete, retarget), and composes changeset.json v3 — an ordered, tool-agnostic operation list with forward-reference encoding — that an external adapter consumes. Pure function over the diff, the caller-supplied tracker listing, the task journal, the spec directory, an optional absorb list, and a caller-supplied git HEAD SHA.

modules.name: ingest
modules.description: Records the outcome of an adapter run. Pure function over changeset.json, receipts.json, the task journal and the spec directory. Appends journal events (change events and task receipts, idempotent by derived event id) and saves the new merkle snapshot when the run is complete. Tolerates partial receipts so unfinished operations resurface on the next plan run via the idempotency path.

modules.name: adapters
modules.description: The adapter contract, plus a reference adapter. The receipts wire-format constants live in a Go package compiled into spex; the adapters themselves are scripts outside the binary. Each adapter consumes changeset.json, executes the tool-specific subcommands against a bead tracker, and writes receipts.json. The current reference adapter targets br (beads_rust); authors of adapters for other trackers (bd, GitHub Issues, Jira) consult the same changeset/receipts contracts without changes to spex. Requirements in this module double as the contract any adapter must satisfy.

modules.name: proposal
modules.description: Proposal lifecycle management: registration, structure validation, history tracking, templates.

modules.name: render
modules.description: Generates human-readable output from spec: collated markdown, graphviz DOT, machine-readable JSON.

modules.name: cli
modules.description: Cross-cutting CLI infrastructure. Provides the root command, the version and hash-id subcommands, and the subcommand registration framework using cobra.

modules.name: map
modules.description: Spec-to-bead correlation layer. Owns access to the task journal that links spec node identity hashes to task ids. Provides journal folds, context resolution, and the CLI query interface.

modules.name: lifecycle
modules.description: Project identity and lifecycle: owns the on-disk contract of what a spex project is — the .spex/ state directory holding the snapshot and the task journal — the explicit init and doctor commands over it, and the single pre-flight resolver every subcommand calls.

modules.name: delivery
modules.description: Tool delivery: trigger-tiered CI carrying the spec gate, a tag-driven release pipeline producing signed and attested cross-architecture binaries, a self-verifying release manifest, and the embedded self-update mechanism spex upgrade drives.
